subject.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken

question: Should Gateway readiness remain true when an enabled configured plugin has a statically verified, exact-root payload failure and is reported as configured-unavailable?
rationale: The branch deliberately replaces the current fail-closed readiness outcome for a class of existing deployments; tests and real proof establish the mechanics but cannot decide the desired operator-facing availability contract.

options.title: Adopt bounded degradation
options.body: Merge the exact-root quarantine policy so healthy Gateway functions continue while the affected plugin is visibly configured-unavailable.

options.title: Keep fail-closed readiness
options.body: Retain the existing behavior where any enabled configured plugin payload verification failure prevents Gateway readiness.

options.title: Defer with an explicit policy design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a broader readiness/readiness-probe contract for partial plugin availability.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded degradation
recommendation.body: Merge the exact-root quarantine policy so healthy Gateway functions continue while the affected plugin is visibly configured-unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: Assignment and the latest hardening commit place steipete closest to the remaining Gateway readiness policy choice.
